narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Tropanka comes from the Dobrudzha region in northeastern Bulgaria.
It was originally performed as a men's dance within traditional rural communities, but later expanded into mixed-gender line formations.
on_screen: Map: Bulgaria · Europe

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally performed by men in village contexts, Tropanka is today performed in mixed social lines, international Bulgarian folk dance ensembles, and educational settings.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers form a line or arc, holding hands while facing inward toward the center.
The movements feature a heavy, earthy posture, distinct foot stamps, and rhythmic pumping arm motions set to 2/4 meter music.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Tropanka (Bulgaria). Meter 2/4. Mood: heavy, earthy, energetic. It should sound like this: Music in 2/4 meter supporting a heavy, earthy rhythm suited for stamping and arm pumping. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
